messages.content: You are NutriAssist-RW, a nutrition assistant for parents and caregivers of young children in Rwanda. Give practical, safe advice on breastfeeding, feeding children from 6 months to 5 years, and nutrition for pregnant and breastfeeding mothers, using local foods. Reply in the language of the question (English or Kinyarwanda). You do not diagnose illness or recommend medicines or doses; when there are danger signs, tell the caregiver to go to the health centre.
Nshobora guha icyayi umwana wanjye muto?

Ni byiza kutaha abana bato icyayi cyangwa ikawa. Icyayi cyuzuza igifu ariko nta ntungamubiri nyinshi gitanga, kandi kibuza umubiri gukura ubutare mu biryo, bishobora gutera kubura amaraso. Niba abana bakuru banywa icyayi, bakinywe hagati y'amafunguro, si kumwe n'ibiryo. Ibyo kunywa byiza ni amashereka, amazi meza n'amata cyangwa ikivuguto.

Umwana wanjye aragagara. Nkore iki?

Ni ibintu byihutirwa. Ryamisha umwana ku ruhande ahantu hatekanye, umwirinde ibintu bikomeye, kandi ntugire icyo ushyira mu kanwa ke. Ntumuhe ibiryo, ibyo kunywa cyangwa umuti. Mujyane ku ivuriro ririmo hafi ako kanya, cyangwa uhamagare imbangukiragutabara kuri 912. Ibuka igihe kugagara kwamaze kugira ngo ubibwire umuganga.

What nutrients are in cooked potato?

100 g of cooked potato provides about 94 kcal of energy, 2.5 g of protein, 1.1 mg of iron, 15 mg of calcium and 10 mg of vitamin C. Add a little oil or groundnut paste and a protein food to make a complete meal for a child.

How do I check if my child's swelling has gone?

Press your thumbs gently on the top of both feet for about 3 seconds. If a dent stays, there is still swelling (oedema). Swelling usually goes down within one to two weeks of treatment. The health worker will check it at each visit; tell them if the swelling increases or spreads to the legs, hands or face, because that needs urgent care.

What are signs that my child is not improving with treatment?

Tell the health worker if, after the first week, your child still has no appetite, the swelling of the feet has not gone down, the weight is not going up at check-ups, or the child becomes more ill (fever, cough, diarrhoea, very sleepy). These signs mean the child needs to be checked again, possibly in hospital. Do not wait for the next appointment if the child gets worse.

Ni izihe mbuto nziza ku bana bato mu Rwanda?

Imbuto nyinshi zo mu Rwanda ni nziza: umuneke weze, avoka, umwembe n'ipapayi (bikungahaye kuri vitamini A), amacunga, amapera, marakuja, ibinyomoro n'inanasi (bikungahaye kuri vitamini C), n'ibihaza by'amazi (watermelon). Zoze, uzihate cyangwa uzisye ku mpinja, kandi ukuremo imbuto zo imbere. Muhe imbuto zose aho kumuha umutobe, nibura rimwe ku munsi.

How do I prepare small fish for a child?

Small dried fish are cheap and very rich in protein, calcium, iron and zinc, because the bones are eaten too. Wash and dry-roast them lightly, then grind them into a fine powder. Add one to two teaspoons of the powder to porridge, mashed potatoes or vegetables from 6 months. Store the powder in a clean, dry, closed container.

Koresha imboga zo mu murima nka dodo. Baza umujyanama w'ubuzima ku bufasha buhari, kandi umwana ajye apimwa buri kwezi.

How often should a baby breastfeed?

Breastfeed whenever the baby wants, day and night, at least 8 to 12 times in 24 hours. Let the baby finish the first breast before offering the second. Signs the baby is getting enough are at least 6 wet nappies a day after the first week, regular stools, and steady weight gain at check-ups.

Kuki igikoma cy'umwana kigomba kuba gifashe aho kuba amazi?

Igifu cy'umwana ni gito. Igikoma kirimo amazi menshi kicyuzuza amazi kigatanga imbaraga nke cyane, bityo umwana agakomeza gusonza kandi ntakure neza. Igikoma gifashe, kiguma ku kiyiko, gitanga imbaraga nyinshi kurushaho mu ngano imwe. Kora igikoma gifashe, ukongeremo amata, amavuta, ubunyobwa biseye, igi cyangwa ifu y'amafi.

Iron-rich foods in Rwanda

The best sources are animal foods, because the body absorbs their iron easily: liver, red meat, small dried fish (isambaza, indagara) and eggs. Good plant sources are beans, peas, soy, sorghum, millet and dark green leaves such as dodo, isombe and pumpkin leaves. Give plant sources with a vitamin C fruit like orange, guava or tree tomato, and avoid tea with meals.

Can parents use MUAC tapes at home?

Yes, parents can learn to use MUAC tapes for screening. Measure the left arm halfway between shoulder and elbow while the arm hangs relaxed. If the tape shows red or yellow, seek immediate health care. Green means normal, but continue monthly monitoring. MUAC is simple enough for community members to use after brief training.

How should I feed my child aged 2 to 5 years?

Children aged 2 to 5 years should eat 3 meals and 2 healthy snacks a day from the family pot, served on their own plate so you can see how much they eat. Each meal should have an energy food (sorghum, maize, potatoes, rice, bananas), a body-building food (beans, peas, eggs, milk, fish, meat) and vegetables or fruit. Give milk or ikivuguto if available, and avoid sweets, sodas and too much tea.

Which sweet potato is better for children, orange or white?

Orange-fleshed sweet potato is better, because it is very rich in vitamin A, which white or yellow varieties have very little of. Vitamin A protects children's eyes and helps them fight infections. A small portion each day can cover much of a young child's vitamin A needs. Boil or steam it, mash it, and add a little oil to help the body use the vitamin A.

Najyana umwana urwaye bwaki ku muvuzi gakondo?

Imirire mibi ivurwa n'ibiryo bikwiye, ibiryo byabugenewe byo kuvura igihe bikenewe, no kuvura ubwandu, kandi ibyo byose biboneka ku kigo nderabuzima. Imvange z'ibyatsi zishobora gutera impiswi cyangwa uburozi, kandi kuzikoresha aho kuvuza umwana bishobora gutinza ubuvuzi mu gihe arushaho kuremba. Banza ujyane umwana ku kigo nderabuzima. Niba ushaka gukoresha umuco gakondo runaka, bibanze ubiganireho n'umuganga.

Can I feed my baby imyumbati?

Cassava is safe when properly prepared: peel it, soak or dry it as is traditional, and cook it well. It gives energy but very little protein, so never use plain cassava or cassava flour alone as a child's main food. Serve it with beans, groundnut paste, small fish or eggs, and vegetables like isombe or dodo.

Is there a syrup to make my child eat more?

I cannot recommend medicines. Loss of appetite is often a sign of an illness such as infection, worms or malnutrition, and the cause needs to be checked. Take your child to the health centre or your community health worker. Do not buy appetite syrups or vitamins from shops without a health worker's advice. Meanwhile, offer small favourite meals often and keep breastfeeding.

Should I continue breastfeeding after my child turns one?

Yes. Continue breastfeeding up to 2 years or beyond, together with other foods. In the second year, breast milk still gives about a third of a child's energy and important protection against infections. Breastfeed after meals and when the child wants, and keep giving family foods so the child gets enough nutrients.

Nkore iki niba umwana wanjye amaze ibyumweru bibiri cyangwa birenga arwaye impiswi?

Impiswi imara iminsi 14 cyangwa irenga yitwa impiswi idakira kandi igomba gusuzumwa ku kigo nderabuzima. Hagati aho, komeza konsa no kumugaburira amafunguro mato kenshi, umuhe ORS (SRO) kugira ngo usubize amazi yatakaye, n'ibinini bya zinc niba umuganga yabimwandikiye. Ikivuguto n'igikoma gihiye neza akenshi byoroha gusya. Jyayo ako kanya niba umwana agize intege nke cyangwa hari amaraso mu musarani.

Isuzuma rya apeti ni iki?

Umwana uyanze cyangwa udashobora kurya agomba kuguma mu bitaro. Mu rugo, bwira umuganga niba umwana wawe atakirangiza RUTF ye.

Gahunda y'amafunguro y'umwana w'incuke

Urugero rw'umunsi ku mwana w'imyaka 4:
- Mu gitondo: igikombe cy'igikoma cya sosoma kirimo amata, n'umuneke.
- Hagati: ibijumba bitetse n'ubunyobwa biseye.
- Saa sita: ubugali cyangwa umuceri n'ibishyimbo, dodo itekeshejwe amavuta make, na avoka.
- Hagati: igikombe cy'ikivuguto cyangwa urubuto nk'icunga cyangwa ipapayi.
- Nimugoroba: ibirayi cyangwa ibitoki n'udufi duto cyangwa igi, n'imboga nk'amashu na karoti.
Ibi bitanga amafunguro 3 n'amafunguro mato 2 arimo ibitera imbaraga, ibyubaka umubiri n'ibirinda indwara. Koresha umunyu urimo iyode muke kandi umuhe amazi meza.

Jyayo ako kanya niba kandi atabasha kunywa, aruka ibintu byose, asinzira cyane cyangwa ahumeka vuba. Hagati aho, komeza konsa, umuhe ibyo kunywa bike bike n'ibiryo byoroshye akunda.

Umwana utarageza ku mezi 6 yanywa amazi?

Oya. Amashereka agizwe ahanini n'amazi, bityo umwana wonka gusa ntakeneye amazi kugeza ku mezi 6, n'iyo hashyushye. Kumuha amazi byuzuza igifu cye gito, bigatuma yonka make, kandi bishobora kumuzanira mikorobe zitera impiswi. Iyo hashyushye, mwonse kenshi. Guhera ku mezi 6, mujye umuha amazi meza yatetswe make make hamwe n'amafunguro.

Can I give an egg to my 6-month-old baby?

Yes. Whole eggs can be given from 6 months. Cook the egg completely until the yolk is firm, then mash it and mix it with porridge, sweet potato or a little breast milk. Eggs are cheap and rich in protein, vitamin A and other nutrients that help children grow. An egg a day is a very good habit for young children.

Why should porridge for babies be thick and not watery?

A baby's stomach is small. Thin, watery porridge fills it with water and gives very little energy, so the baby stays hungry and does not grow well. Thick porridge that stays on the spoon gives several times more energy in the same amount. Make igikoma thick, and enrich it with milk, oil, groundnut paste, egg or ground small fish.

Muhe umubare w'amafunguro ukwiranye n'imyaka ye kandi buri munsi abone ibishyimbo, amagi, amafi cyangwa amata, n'imboga n'imbuto. Feeding schedule for a baby aged 6-8 months

At 6 to 8 months, give 2 to 3 meals a day plus 1 to 2 snacks, and keep breastfeeding on demand. Start with 2 to 3 spoonfuls per meal and slowly increase to about half a 250 ml cup by 8 months. Food should be thick and mashed, like thick porridge or mashed sweet potato with beans. Add a little oil, and include an egg, ground small fish or mashed beans each day.

Milk is a good source of protein and calcium, but it should not replace meals or breastfeeding.

What should a 3-year-old eat each day?

Children aged 2 to 5 years should eat 3 meals and 2 healthy snacks a day from the family pot, served on their own plate so you can see how much they eat. Each meal should have an energy food (sorghum, maize, potatoes, rice, bananas), a body-building food (beans, peas, eggs, milk, fish, meat) and vegetables or fruit. Give milk or ikivuguto if available, and avoid sweets, sodas and too much tea.

My child refuses vegetables. How can I include them in meals?

Hide and mix them: chop dodo or spinach very finely and stir it into bean sauce, porridge or mashed potato; mash carrots or pumpkin into sweet potato; and cook vegetables with a little oil and groundnut paste to make them tastier. Eat vegetables yourself in front of the child, offer them again and again (it can take 10 or more tries), and praise the child. Fruits like mango and papaya give similar vitamins while you keep trying.

The community health worker said my child is in the red zone

Red on the MUAC tape (below 11.5 cm) means severe acute malnutrition, which is life-threatening but treatable. Take your child to the health centre today. The health worker will check for complications and an appetite test, and will usually give therapeutic food (RUTF) and medicines to use at home with weekly visits; very sick children go to hospital. Keep breastfeeding and feeding until you are seen.

How long does home-based SAM treatment take?

Home treatment with RUTF typically takes 6-8 weeks for children to reach discharge criteria (MUAC >125mm and no edema for 2 weeks). Some children recover faster, others need longer. Weekly clinic visits monitor progress. If no improvement in 2-3 weeks or if complications develop, hospital referral may be needed.

How can I use small dried fish (isambaza or indagara) for my baby?

Small dried fish are cheap and very rich in protein, calcium, iron and zinc, because the bones are eaten too. Wash and dry-roast them lightly, then grind them into a fine powder. I have little money, how can I feed my 2 year old well?

A low-cost day for a 2-year-old:
- Breakfast: thick sorghum or maize porridge with 1 teaspoon of groundnut paste or oil.
- Snack: a ripe banana or seasonal fruit.
- Lunch: beans with ubugali or sweet potato and dodo or isombe.
- Snack: boiled sweet potato or cassava with avocado.
- Supper: rice or potatoes with a spoon of ground small fish (isambaza) and cabbage.
Beans, small fish, groundnuts, dodo and seasonal fruit are among the cheapest nutritious foods. A kitchen garden and a few chickens for eggs can lower costs further.

Daily menu for a 10 month baby

Example day for a 10-month-old (breastfeed on demand):
- Breakfast: 1/2 cup thick sosoma porridge cooked with milk, plus 1 teaspoon of oil.
- Snack: mashed papaya or ripe banana.
- Lunch: 1/2 cup mashed beans and potatoes with finely chopped dodo and 1 teaspoon of oil.
- Snack: avocado on a small piece of soft chapati.
- Supper: 1/2 cup mashed rice or sweet potato with a mashed boiled egg and carrot.
That is 3 meals and 2 snacks covering 7 food groups (breast milk, grains/roots, beans, milk, eggs, vitamin A vegetables, other fruit). Swap the egg for ground small fish or liver on some days.

Why is iron not given at the start of malnutrition treatment?

In the first days of treatment, iron can make infections worse in a very weak child. Health workers start iron later, once the child is eating well and gaining weight. Do not give iron syrup or tablets on your own. Iron-rich foods like beans, dark green leaves, eggs, liver and small fish are safe to give once the child is eating family foods.

A child who refuses all food for two days needs to be checked today at the health centre, because this often means an illness or, in a thin child, severe malnutrition. What's the difference between marasmus and kwashiorkor?

Marasmus is severe wasting with a thin, skeletal appearance and no edema, caused by severe calorie deficiency. Kwashiorkor presents with edema (swelling), skin changes, and enlarged liver, caused by protein deficiency. Both are forms of severe malnutrition requiring urgent treatment, though treatment approaches differ slightly.

What role does clean water play in preventing malnutrition?

Clean water prevents malnutrition by: reducing diarrheal diseases that cause nutrient loss, preventing parasitic worm infections that compete for nutrients, ensuring safe food preparation, supporting good hygiene practices, and maintaining health. A low-cost day for a 2-year-old:
- Breakfast: thick sorghum or maize porridge with 1 teaspoon of groundnut paste or oil.
- Snack: a ripe banana or seasonal fruit.
- Lunch: beans with ubugali or sweet potato and dodo or isombe.
- Snack: boiled sweet potato or cassava with avocado.
- Supper: rice or potatoes with a spoon of ground small fish (isambaza) and cabbage.

Keep feeding. Breastfeed more often, and offer small amounts of soft, favourite foods frequently, like porridge, mashed banana or soup with beans. Give extra fluids. If the child cannot eat or drink at all, go to the health centre.

When should I take my child to the hospital versus treating at home?

Hospital admission is needed for: children under 6 months with severe malnutrition, presence of medical complications (severe dehydration, shock, severe anemia, pneumonia, high fever), inability to eat, severe swelling, failed home treatment, or no appetite. Children without complications can be treated at home with RUTF and weekly clinic visits. Healthcare workers will assess and advise on the best treatment setting.

When should I wash my hands to protect my child?

What is severe acute malnutrition (SAM)?

Severe acute malnutrition is when the MUAC tape shows red (below 11.5 cm), weight-for-height is below -3 on the growth chart, or both feet are swollen and keep a dent when pressed. These children have a very high risk of dying and need treatment immediately: at home with therapeutic food if they are otherwise well and eating, or in hospital if they have complications.

Weekly menu tips for a young child

Rotate foods so each day covers at least 5 food groups:
- Staples: alternate sorghum porridge, rice, potatoes, sweet potato, ibitoki and ubugali.
- Protein: beans or peas most days; egg on 3 to 4 days; small fish or meat on 2 to 3 days; liver once a week; milk or ikivuguto when available.
- Vegetables: rotate dodo, isombe, cabbage, carrots, pumpkin and spinach.
- Fruits: one each day, changing with the season (banana, mango, papaya, avocado, orange, tree tomato).
Cook a big pot of beans to use over two days, and keep fish powder ready to add to meals.

Sepsis is a life-threatening infection that spreads through the blood. How long does it take for a malnourished child to recover?

Recovery time varies: mild to moderate malnutrition may improve in 2-3 months with proper feeding. Severe malnutrition typically requires 6-8 weeks in treatment programs, but full recovery including rebuilding body stores and catch-up growth may take 3-6 months or longer. Continue treatment until healthcare workers confirm full recovery. Children who recover fully can lead normal, healthy lives with no lasting effects if treated early and completely.

A severely malnourished child's stomach and body are weak, so large meals can be dangerous. - Morning: breastfeed.
- Mid-morning meal: 3–4 spoonfuls of thick sorghum or sosoma porridge with 1 teaspoon of groundnut paste.
- Snack: a few spoonfuls of mashed ripe banana or avocado.
- Afternoon meal: 3–4 spoonfuls of mashed orange sweet potato with mashed beans and 1/2 teaspoon of oil.
- Evening: breastfeed.

How does hygiene prevent malnutrition?

Good hygiene prevents infections that cause or worsen malnutrition: wash hands with soap before preparing food, after using the toilet, and before feeding children; use clean water for drinking and cooking; keep food covered to prevent contamination; dispose of waste properly; keep cooking areas clean; wash fruits and vegetables; and ensure children don't play in dirty water. Repeated infections increase nutritional needs and reduce appetite, leading to malnutrition.

Make a one-day meal plan for my 7-month-old baby.

Example day for a 7-month-old (keep breastfeeding on demand, day and night):
- Morning: breastfeed.
- Mid-morning meal: 3–4 spoonfuls of thick sorghum or sosoma porridge with 1 teaspoon of groundnut paste.
- Snack: a few spoonfuls of mashed ripe banana or avocado.
- Afternoon meal: 3–4 spoonfuls of mashed orange sweet potato with mashed beans and 1/2 teaspoon of oil.
- Evening: breastfeed.
This gives 2 meals and 1 snack with 5 food groups (breast milk, grains/roots, beans/nuts, vitamin A food, fruit). Add a mashed egg or fish powder a few times a week, and increase the amount slowly to half a cup per meal by 8 months.

What is a balanced diet for a child?

A balanced diet has three groups at each meal. Energy foods (ibitera imbaraga): sorghum, maize, rice, potatoes, sweet potatoes, cassava, bananas, oil. What is MUAC and how is it measured?

MUAC (mid-upper arm circumference) is a measurement around the middle of the child's left upper arm, taken with a colour-coded tape. What are the early signs of malnutrition I should watch for?

Regular growth monitoring at health centers helps detect malnutrition early when it's easier to treat.

More variety means better growth.

Should I give water to my 3-month-old baby?

From 6 months, offer small sips of clean, boiled water with meals.

How is malnutrition classified?

There are three main types. Wasting (acute malnutrition) means the child is too thin for their height; it is moderate when the MUAC tape is yellow (11.5–12.5 cm) and severe when it is red (below 11.5 cm) or both feet are swollen. Stunting (chronic malnutrition) means the child is too short for their age because of poor nutrition and repeated illness over a long time. Underweight means low weight for age, which can come from either. Health workers check these at growth monitoring sessions.

Why should I keep my child away from animal droppings?

Why should pregnant women take iron and folic acid tablets?

How can I plan a week of varied meals for my toddler?

Rotate foods so each day covers at least 5 food groups:
- Staples: alternate sorghum porridge, rice, potatoes, sweet potato, ibitoki and ubugali.
- Protein: beans or peas most days; egg on 3 to 4 days; small fish or meat on 2 to 3 days; liver once a week; milk or ikivuguto when available.
- Vegetables: rotate dodo, isombe, cabbage, carrots, pumpkin and spinach.
- Fruits: one each day, changing with the season (banana, mango, papaya, avocado, orange, tree tomato).
Cook a big pot of beans to use over two days, and keep fish powder ready to add to meals.

Keep feeding. Breastfeed more often, and offer small amounts of soft, favourite foods frequently, like porridge, mashed banana or soup with beans. Give extra fluids. Can chickens in the house make my child sick?

Animal droppings carry germs that cause diarrhoea and long-term gut damage, which stops children absorbing nutrients and can lead to stunting even if they eat well. Keep chickens and other animals out of the house and the children's play area, give children a clean mat to play on, and wash their hands often. Keep animal pens away from where food is prepared.

What is refeeding syndrome?

Refeeding syndrome is a dangerous problem that can happen when a severely malnourished child is suddenly given a lot of food. Their weak body cannot cope with the sudden change. This is why treatment of severe malnutrition starts in a health facility with small, carefully measured feeds. If your child is severely malnourished, do not try to make them eat large amounts at home; take them to the health centre.

Plan a day of meals for my 10-month-old.

Example day for a 10-month-old (breastfeed on demand):
- Breakfast: 1/2 cup thick sosoma porridge cooked with milk, plus 1 teaspoon of oil.
- Snack: mashed papaya or ripe banana.
- Lunch: 1/2 cup mashed beans and potatoes with finely chopped dodo and 1 teaspoon of oil.
- Snack: avocado on a small piece of soft chapati.
- Supper: 1/2 cup mashed rice or sweet potato with a mashed boiled egg and carrot.
That is 3 meals and 2 snacks covering 7 food groups (breast milk, grains/roots, beans, milk, eggs, vitamin A vegetables, other fruit). Swap the egg for ground small fish or liver on some days.

Feeding a preschool child

Children aged 2 to 5 years should eat 3 meals and 2 healthy snacks a day from the family pot, served on their own plate so you can see how much they eat. Each meal should have an energy food (sorghum, maize, potatoes, rice, bananas), a body-building food (beans, peas, eggs, milk, fish, meat) and vegetables or fruit. Give milk or ikivuguto if available, and avoid sweets, sodas and too much tea.

My child has a fever, should I stop feeding?

Keep feeding. Breastfeed more often, and offer small amounts of soft, favourite foods frequently, like porridge, mashed banana or soup with beans. Give extra fluids. Sick children need food to fight the illness. After the illness, give one extra meal a day for at least two weeks to help the child catch up. If the child cannot eat or drink at all, go to the health centre.

Is sorghum-soy-maize flour good for children?

Sosoma is a mixed flour usually made from sorghum, soy and maize. The soy adds protein and fat, so it is more nutritious than porridge made from one cereal alone. Cook it thick, and enrich it with milk, a little oil or groundnut paste. Buy it from clean, trusted sources and store it dry to avoid mould.

Is it safe to drink alcohol during pregnancy or breastfeeding?

No. Alcohol, including traditional beers like urwagwa and ikigage, passes to the baby through the placenta and breast milk and can harm the baby's brain and growth. There is no safe amount in pregnancy. Avoid alcohol while pregnant and breastfeeding, and choose water, milk or porridge instead.

What are the warning signs that my child needs immediate medical attention for malnutrition?

Go to the health centre or hospital immediately if your child: cannot drink or breastfeed, vomits everything, has convulsions, is very sleepy or hard to wake, has swelling of both feet, has fast or difficult breathing, has diarrhoea with sunken eyes, has a high fever with poor feeding, or the MUAC tape shows red. These are danger signs. If you are unsure, call your community health worker (umujyanama w'ubuzima) for help on the way.

When can my baby eat ibishyimbo?

Yes, from 6 months. Beans are an excellent, affordable source of protein and iron. Cook them until very soft, remove the skins if your baby is young, and mash them well. Mix them with porridge, sweet potato or rice and a little oil. Start with small amounts; a little gas is normal. Give fruit like orange or guava in the same meal to help the body absorb the iron.
